SPHERICAL HARMONICS.

$$\begin{aligned}
\Psi=h_{0}+h_{1} & Y_{1} r+\text { \&c. }+h_{n}^{(\sigma)} Y_{n}^{(\sigma)} r^{n}+\ldots \\
& +k_{0}^{1}+k_{1} Y_{1} \frac{1}{r^{2}}+\text { \&c. }+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} Y_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{r^{n+1}}+\cdots,
\end{aligned}$$
(21)
then we have to determine the constants of the forms $h$ and $k$ so
that when $r=a(1+F), \Psi=a$, and when $r=b(1+G), \Psi=\beta$.
It is manifest, from our former investigation, that all the $h$ 's
and $k$ 's except $h_{0}$ and $k_{0}$ will be small quantities, the products of
which into $F$ may be neglected. We may, therefore, write
$$\begin{aligned}
& a=h_{0}+k_{0} \frac{1}{a}(1-F)+\text { \&c. }+\left(h_{n}^{(\sigma)} u^{n}+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{a^{n+1}}\right) Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}+\cdots \\
& \beta=h_{0}+k_{0} \frac{1}{b}(1-G)+\text { \&c. }+\left(h_{n}^{(\sigma)} b^{n}+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{b^{n+1}}\right) Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}+\cdots
\end{aligned}$$
(22)
(23)
We have therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
a & =h_{0}+k_{0} \frac{1}{a} \\
\beta & =h_{0}+k_{0} \frac{1}{b} \\
k_{0} \frac{1}{a} f_{n}^{(\sigma)} & =h_{n}^{(\sigma)} u^{n}+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{a^{n+1}} \\
k_{0} \frac{1}{b} g_{n}^{(\sigma)} & =h_{n}^{(\sigma)} b^{n}+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{b^{n+1}}
\end{aligned}$$
(24)
(25)
(26)
(27)
whence we find for $k_{0}$, the charge of the inner conductor,
$$k_{0}=(\alpha-\beta) \frac{a b}{b-a}$$
(28)
and for the coefficients of the harmonics of order $n$
$$\begin{aligned}
& h_{n}^{(\sigma)}=k_{0} \frac{b^{n} g_{n}^{(\sigma)}-a^{n} f_{n}^{(\sigma)}}{b^{2 n+1}-a^{2 n+1}} \\
& k_{n}^{(\sigma)}=k_{0} a^{n} b^{n} \frac{b^{n+1} f_{n}^{(\sigma)}-a^{n+1} g_{n}^{(\sigma)}}{b^{2 n+1}-a^{2 n+1}}
\end{aligned}$$
(29)
(30)
where we must remember that the coefficients $f_{n}^{(\sigma)}, g_{n}^{(\tau)}, h_{n}^{(\sigma)}, k_{n}^{(\sigma)}$ are
those belonging to the same type as well as order.
The surface density on the inner conductor is given by the
equation
$$4 \pi \sigma a^{2}=k_{0}\left(1+\ldots+A_{n} Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}+\ldots\right)$$
where $A_{n}=\frac{f_{n}^{(\sigma)}\left\{(n+2) a^{2 n+1}+(n-1) b^{2 n+1}\right\}-g_{n}^{(\sigma)}(2 n+1) a^{n+1} b^{n}}{b^{2 n+1}-a^{2 n+1}}$.
(31)
146.] As an example of the application of zonal harmonics,
let us investigate the equilibrium of electricity on two spherical
conductors.

$$\begin{align*}
\Psi=h_{0}+h_{1} & Y_{1} r+\text { \&c. }+h_{n}^{(\sigma)} Y_{n}^{(\sigma)} r^{n}+\ldots \\
& +k_{0}^{1}+k_{1} Y_{1} \frac{1}{r^{2}}+\text { \&c. }+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} Y_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{r^{n+1}}+\cdots, \tag{21}
\end{align*}$$

then we have to determine the constants of the forms $h$ and $k$ so
 that when $r=a(1+F), \Psi=a$, and when $r=b(1+G), \Psi=\beta$.


It is manifest, from our former investigation, that all the $h$ 's
 and $k$ 's except $h_{0}$ and $k_{0}$ will be small quantities, the products of
 which into $F$ may be neglected. We may, therefore, write

$$\begin{align*}
& a=h_{0}+k_{0} \frac{1}{a}(1-F)+\text { \&c. }+\left(h_{n}^{(\sigma)} u^{n}+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{a^{n+1}}\right) Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}+\cdots  \tag{22}\\
& \beta=h_{0}+k_{0} \frac{1}{b}(1-G)+\text { \&c. }+\left(h_{n}^{(\sigma)} b^{n}+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{b^{n+1}}\right) Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}+\cdots \tag{23}
\end{align*}$$


We have therefore

$$\begin{align*}
a & =h_{0}+k_{0} \frac{1}{a}  \tag{24}\\
\beta & =h_{0}+k_{0} \frac{1}{b}  \tag{25}\\
k_{0} \frac{1}{a} f_{n}^{(\sigma)} & =h_{n}^{(\sigma)} u^{n}+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{a^{n+1}}  \tag{26}\\
k_{0} \frac{1}{b} g_{n}^{(\sigma)} & =h_{n}^{(\sigma)} b^{n}+k_{n}^{(\sigma)} \frac{1}{b^{n+1}} \tag{27}
\end{align*}$$

whence we find for $k_{0}$, the charge of the inner conductor,

$$\begin{equation*}
k_{0}=(\alpha-\beta) \frac{a b}{b-a} \tag{28}
\end{equation*}$$

and for the coefficients of the harmonics of order $n$

$$\begin{align*}
& h_{n}^{(\sigma)}=k_{0} \frac{b^{n} g_{n}^{(\sigma)}-a^{n} f_{n}^{(\sigma)}}{b^{2 n+1}-a^{2 n+1}}  \tag{29}\\
& k_{n}^{(\sigma)}=k_{0} a^{n} b^{n} \frac{b^{n+1} f_{n}^{(\sigma)}-a^{n+1} g_{n}^{(\sigma)}}{b^{2 n+1}-a^{2 n+1}} \tag{30}
\end{align*}$$

where we must remember that the coefficients $f_{n}^{(\sigma)}, g_{n}^{(\tau)}, h_{n}^{(\sigma)}, k_{n}^{(\sigma)}$ are
 those belonging to the same type as well as order.


The surface density on the inner conductor is given by the
 equation

$$\begin{equation*}
4 \pi \sigma a^{2}=k_{0}\left(1+\ldots+A_{n} Y_{n}^{(\sigma)}+\ldots\right) \tag{31}
\end{equation*}$$

where $A_{n}=\frac{f_{n}^{(\sigma)}\left\{(n+2) a^{2 n+1}+(n-1) b^{2 n+1}\right\}-g_{n}^{(\sigma)}(2 n+1) a^{n+1} b^{n}}{b^{2 n+1}-a^{2 n+1}}$.

 let us investigate the equilibrium of electricity on two spherical
 conductors.
